He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]]. ==High school career== Blair attended [[St. Edmund Campion Secondary School]] in [[Brampton|Brampton, Ontario]] before completing his high school career at the [[Athlete Institute]] in [[Mono, Ontario]], where he averaged 23.6 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game. He was named most valuable player of the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game and the [[BioSteel All-Canadian Basketball Game|BioSteel All-Canadian Game]].{{cite web |last1=Colpitts |first1=Iain |title=Brampton's Jahvon Blair named Big East's freshman of the week |url=https://www.bramptonguardian.com/community-story/8042125-brampton-s-jahvon-blair-named-big-east-s-freshman-of-the-week/ |website=[[Brampton Guardian]] |access-date=March 18, 2021 |date=January 10, 2018}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], becoming the first commitment during the tenure of head coach [[Patrick Ewing]].{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Jahvon Blair to Georgetown |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2017/04/21/jahvon-blair-georgetown/ |website=Zagsblog |access-date=March 18, 2021 |date=April 21, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman at Georgetown, Blair averaged nine points and was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite web |last1=Copeland |first1=Kareem |title=Jamorko Pickett and Jahvon Blair have been through just about everything at Georgetown |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/02/26/jamorko-pickett-jahvon-blair-last-standing/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=March 18, 2021 |date=February 26, 2021}} He declined to 4.1 points per game in his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=Kostka |first1=Andy |title=Jahvon Blair is Georgetown basketball's keystone on a team full of new faces |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2020/nov/30/jahvon-blair-georgetown-basketballs-keystone-team-/ |website=[[The Washington Times]] |access-date=March 18, 2021 |date=November 30, 2020}} On February 8, 2020, Blair scored a career-high 30 points in a 76–72 win over [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]].{{cite web |title=Blair scores 30, Georgetown rallies to beat DePaul 76-72 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story?id=28660234&src=desktop |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=March 18, 2021 |date=February 8, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 10.8 points per game.{{cite web |last1=Copeland |first1=Kareem |title=Georgetown basketball searching for a new identity after troubled year |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/11/24/georgetown-basketball-season-preview/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=March 18, 2021 |date=November 24, 2020}} In his senior season, Blair assumed a leading role with the departures of several key players, including [[Mac McClung]]. He led the team in scoring with 15.4 points per game and helped lead the Hoyas to the Big East tournament title and Georgetown's first NCAA tournament berth since 2015. After the season, Blair declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing an additional season of eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Copeland |first1=Kareem |title=Georgetown guard Jahvon Blair declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/04/21/jahvon-blair-nba-draft/ |access-date=June 22, 2021 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |date=April 21, 2021}} ==Professional career== On August 23, 2021, Blair signed his first professional contract with [[G.S. Lavrio B.C.|Lavrio]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]].{{cite web |title=Lavrio announces signing of rookie Jahvon Blair |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lavrio-announces-signing-of-rookie-jahvon-blair/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 23, 2021 |date=August 23, 2021}} On January 16, 2022, he signed with [[KTP Basket]] of the [[Korisliiga]].{{cite web |last1=Chelidze |first1=Dimitri |title=Jahvon Blair (ex Lavrio) signs at KTP Basket |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/726930/Jahvon-Blair-(ex-Lavrio)-signs-at-KTP-Basket |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 16, 2022 |date=January 16, 2022}} ===Westchester Knicks (2022)=== On October 23, 2022, Blair joined the [[Westchester Knicks]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/westchester-knicks-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5892760|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} He was then later waived on November 14, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=November 14, 2022|access-date=November 14, 2022}} ===Niagara River Lions (2023)=== On April 13, 2023, Blair signed with the [[Niagara River Lions]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=River Lions Sign Canadian Guard Jahvon Blair|url=https://www.riverlions.ca/blairsigned|website=RiverLions.ca|date=April 13, 2023|access-date=June 14, 2023}} On December 14, 2023, Blair joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], but was waived the next day.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Delaware Blue Coats Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Delaware-Blue-Coats/57/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 15, 2023}} ===Ostioneros de Guaymas (2024)=== Blair signed with the [[Ostioneros de Guaymas (basketball)|Ostioneros de Guaymas]] of the [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico]] (CIBACOPA) ahead of the [[2024 CIBACOPA season]].{{cite news|url=https://cibacopa.org/noticias/gran-presentacion-de-ostioneros/|title=Gran presentación de Ostioneros|publisher=[[CIBACOPA]]|date=February 28, 2024|access-date=March 1, 2024|language=es}} He earned CIBACOPA All-Star honors.{{cite news|url=https://lineadirectaportal.com/deportes/todo-listo-estos-son-los-jugadores-que-participaran-en-el-juego-de-estrellas-cibacopa-2024-2024-04-12__1097684|title=¡Todo listo! Estos son los jugadores que participarán en el Juego de Estrellas Cibacopa 2024|first=Oscar|last=Arrieta|work=Línea Directa Portal |date=12 April 2024|access-date=14 April 2024|language=es}} ===Return to Niagara (2024)=== On February 29, 2024, Blair agreed to return to the [[Niagara River Lions]] for a second stint.{{cite web|title=River Lions Welcome Back Top 4 Leading Scorers from 2023|url=https://www.riverlions.ca/topfourscorersreturn|website=RiverLions.ca|date=February 29, 2024|access-date=August 11, 2024}} ===Poitiers Basket 86 (2024–2025)=== On June 26, 2024, Blair signed with [[Poitiers Basket 86]] of the [[LNB Pro B]].{{cite web|title=Jahvon BLAIR rejoint le PB86|url=https://www.pb86.fr/jahvon-blair-rejoint-le-pb86/|website=PB86.fr|access-date=October 15, 2024|language=French}} ===Chorale Roanne Basket (2025–present)=== On June 20, 2025, he signed with [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.usbasket.com/Canada/news/938895/Jahvon-Henry-Blair-joins-Roanne|title=Jahvon Henry-Blair joins Roanne|last=|first=|date=June 20, 2025|website=|publisher=usbasket|language=En|access-date=July 6, 2026}} ==National team career== Blair represented [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Canada]] at the [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. He averaged 6.8 points and helped his team win the silver medal.{{cite web |title=Jahvon Michael Henry-Blair (CAN)'s profile - FIBA Americas U18 Championship for Men 2016 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/americas/u18/2016/player/Jahvon-Michael-Henry-Blair |website=[[FIBA]] |access-date=March 18, 2021}} Blair later represented the [[Canada men's national basketball
